title: File lock client: local and remote advisory locks
goal: Advisory file locks for parallel agents: a local registry for agents on this machine and a remote protocol client for `file.lock` events so teammates' agents see who is touching which file, without the relay ever learning paths.
scope_in: Path normalisation to a canonical key: relative to the agent's worktree root, POSIX separators, NFC, lowercased on case-insensitive filesystems (macOS, Windows), `..` rejected.
Local registry: in-memory map plus lock files `.centcom/locks/<hash>.json` created with `O_EXCL`, containing pid, agent id, expires_at; stale locks (dead pid or expired) are reclaimed.
`LockClient.acquire(path, { agentId, ttlMs })` default ttl 120 000 ms (max 600 000), auto-renew at ttl/2 while the agent is running; `release`; `releaseAll(agentId)` on agent exit/crash.

Remote protocol: publishes `file.lock` events via an injected `LockTransport.publish(payload)` with clear part `{ action: 'acquire'|'release'|'deny'|'expire', path_hmac, agent_id, ttl_ms? }` and secret `{ path }`; `path_hmac` computed by an injected `PathMac(path) -> base64url string` (BLAKE2b-MAC with the epoch path key from the crypto lane, per CT-CRYPTO key table).

Inbound handling `onRemoteLock(evt)`: maintains a remote table keyed by `path_hmac` (arbitration is by hash; the arbiter/ordering is the relay `seq`), expires entries by `ttl_ms`; `conflicts()` lists locally touched files that a remote agent also holds.

Modes (`lock.mode` config): `warn` (default; acquire always succeeds but returns `heldBy`), `block` (acquire fails with `LockHeld` and the permission engine denies the edit with reason `file_locked`). Emits `lock:changed` and `lock:conflict` on the bus and a `conflict.detected` payload builder `{ agent_ids, path_hmacs }`.
Works offline/LAN: with no transport (solo), only the local registry is active.
scope_out: Key derivation and the HMAC primitive: crypto lane (injected `PathMac`).
Sending frames and sequencing: session lanes; relay arbitration: the real relay.
Editing enforcement inside tools: lane C015 consults `LockClient.check` via a hook; no tool wrapping here.
build_against: Local tests use a temp worktree from lane C017's helper or a plain temp dir, an in-memory `LockTransport` that loops frames, and the mock backend (lane C007) relay simulator for sequencing of `file.lock` frames in an integration test with two simulated clients.
interfaces: `createLockClient(deps: { root: string; fs: LockFs; clock: Clock; bus: AgentBus; pathMac?: (relPath: string) => string; transport?: LockTransport; config: { mode: 'warn'|'block'; defaultTtlMs: number } }): LockClient`

`interface LockClient { acquire(path: string, o: { agentId: AgentId; ttlMs?: number }): Promise<LockResult>; release(path: string, agentId: AgentId): Promise<void>; releaseAll(agentId: AgentId): Promise<void>; check(path: string): LockInfo | null; onRemoteLock(evt: FileLockPayload): void; conflicts(): Conflict[] }`

`type LockResult = { ok: true; heldBy?: AgentId } | { ok: false; reason: 'held'; heldBy: AgentId; expiresAt: string }`; `interface LockTransport { publish(p: { clear: FileLockPayload; secret: { path: string } }): void }`.
acceptance: Two agents acquiring the same file: in `warn` mode both get `ok:true` and the second receives `heldBy` = first; in `block` mode the second gets `ok:false, reason:'held'`.
Path keys: `src/A.ts` and `src/a.ts` collide on macOS/Windows settings and not on Linux; `../x`, absolute paths and paths escaping via symlink are rejected with `PathOutsideRoot`.
Lock auto-renews at 60 000 ms for a 120 000 ms ttl (fake clock) and emits `expire` exactly once if the agent stops renewing; `releaseAll` on agent exit releases every lock within one tick.
A stale lock file whose pid is dead is reclaimed; a live pid's lock is not; `O_EXCL` race between two processes yields exactly one winner (child-process test).
Published frames: clear part validates against the generated `file.lock` clear schema, contains `path_hmac` but never the path; the secret part is only passed to the transport.
A remote `acquire` for a path the local agent has edited produces one `lock:conflict` bus event and one `conflict.detected` payload with both agent ids and the hash.
Remote entries expire after `ttl_ms` even if no release arrives; unknown `action` values are ignored with a debug log.
With no transport configured, 1,000 acquire/release cycles complete in < 500 ms and send nothing.
tests: normalize.test.ts (case, NFC, traversal, symlink), local-registry.test.ts (EXCL race, stale, renew).
two-client integration test against the relay simulator.
guardrails: Locks are ADVISORY: MUST NOT corrupt, delete or chmod user files and MUST NOT hold OS-level file locks that can block other tools.
The relay-visible part MUST be `path_hmac` only; the real path travels only inside the encrypted secret payload; MUST NOT log paths or hashes together with paths.
MUST NOT block the agent indefinitely: `block` mode fails fast; every wait has a timeout (default 5 s).
MUST NOT reuse a path MAC across epochs incorrectly: recompute using the current key id after `control.rotate_key` (receivers compare hashes per `kid`).
Remote events from non-members/unknown devices MUST be ignored (membership comes from the roster given by the session layer).
failure_modes: Transport down -> local locks continue; remote publication is queued (bounded 200 events, drop oldest) and flushed on reconnect.
Clock skew between machines -> remote expiry uses the receiver's clock from receipt time + `ttl_ms`, never sender timestamps.
Lock dir not writable -> in-memory locks only with one warning.
notes: TTL values are product choices (contract only says `ttl_ms` optional).
